podcast.title: Libel Suit Against London Daily Mirror (1959)
podcast.body: Liberace, a famous pianist, sued the London Daily Mirror for libel in 1959 after the newspaper implied he was gay. During the trial, under oath, he denied ever indulging in homosexual practices. The judge believed him and awarded him $24,000 in damages. "He had never indulged in any homosexual practices."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Palimony Suit from Bodyguard (1982)
podcast.body: In 1982, a former male bodyguard sued Liberace for palimony. This time, Liberace was ordered to pay out $95,000 from his bank account. "Liberace had to pay out $95,000 from his bank account."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Death from AIDS and Daily Mirror's Reaction (1987)
podcast.body: Liberace died of AIDS in 1987. Following his death, the Daily Mirror reportedly "came calling, looking for a refund of their $24,000" that they had been ordered to pay him in the 1959 libel case. "he died of AIDS, and the Daily Mirror came calling, looking for a refund of their $24,000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Acceptance as Performance
podcast.body: Liberace's popularity with mainstream audiences was attributed to the perception of his persona as "theater" or "performance," which allowed audiences to enjoy his act without confronting his personal life. "We explain the village people the same way that we explain grandma loving the barachi."
